title: Up! Go! More!

note_to_grownups.heading: A note for grown-ups
draft: This book is small on purpose. One word, one picture and one thing to copy on each page, so there is room for the most important part: the two of you, taking turns.
You don’t need to read every tip, finish the book or get anything right. Go slow. Wait. Copy your child’s sounds and moves, and let them copy yours. That back-and-forth is the whole idea.
Thank you for reading with your little one.

tip: Take turns.
Say “hi!” and count to five in your head. A look, wave or sound back counts as a turn.
Build the pause.
Hide, wait a beat, then pop out. In time, your child may fill that pause with a squeal or a sound.
Wait for it.
Hold your arms out, then pause. When they reach up, say “up!” as you lift.
Say it big.
Crouch low and stretch the word out. Slow, playful words are easier to copy.
Leave a gap.
Say “Ready, set…” then stop and wait. Let your child fill in “go!” Any sound counts.
Make it a game.
Zoom a toy car and freeze on “stop!” Then let your child be the one who says it.
Add one word.
If your child says “ball,” you say “big ball” or “roll ball.” Just one step ahead.
Repeat it.
Drop blocks in one at a time: “in… in… in!” Words heard again and again are easier to try.

cue: Close your hands, then pop them open
tip: Wait for a signal.
Hold the box shut and wait. A look, a tap or a sound tells you what they want.
Say what you see.
Look where your child looks and name it: “Wow! Big sun!” Short and bright beats long and busy.
Name the moment.
Little tumbles are talk moments. Say “uh-oh!” with a big face, then wait.

cue: Thumbs-up on open palm, lift up
tip: Set up a reason to ask.
Put a favorite toy just out of reach and wait. A reach, point or sound is asking.
Copy them.
Clap back the way your child claps: fast, slow, loud or soft. Copying says “I’m listening.”
Follow their lead.
Grabbed a shoe? Talk about the shoe: “Your shoe. Big shoe. Shoe on!”
Talk about now.
Name what is happening at the table as it happens: “Eat. You eat. Yum!”
Keep it short.
Two or three words at a time: “Cup. Your cup. Sip!” Short phrases are easy to copy.
Pause the fun.
Stop the bubbles, ask “more?” and wait. A sign, a look or a sound means go again.

cue: Open hands up, twist back and forth
tip: Offer a choice.
“More, or all done?” Hold up a hand for each. A point is a real answer.
Make it a routine.
Same wave, same words, every time. Words that repeat are the easiest to pick up.
Let them turn.
Let your child turn the pages and choose where to stop. Name whatever they point at.
Sing it.
Put “hug” in any tune you know and squeeze on the last one. Not a hugger? A high five works too.
Wind down.
Say “night-night” to everything: the duck, the moon, even the tablet. A calm goodnight game.
